extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy/aesthetics; scholars of art theory
extracted.subtask_description: Philosophical criteria for evaluating aesthetic objects and works of art, distinguishing the beautiful from the sublime, diagnosing degrees of aesthetic effect, and specifying implications for painting, sculpture, architecture, and moral character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Light as condition of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Light is 'the pleasantest and most gladdening of things' and is the indispensable condition of beauty because it is the correlative and condition of the most perfect kind of perceptive knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the presence, quality, and disposition of light facilitate 'pure knowing' (objective perception free from will). Examples: favourable light enhances architectural beauty and can lift contemplation into a state of pure knowing; reflected rays (e.g., objects in water) produce special aesthetic delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure from perception (will-less knowing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pleasure of sight arises from the objective possibility of pure perceptive knowledge, which does not directly affect the will, unlike tastes and smells which are closely related to will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether aesthetic pleasure stems primarily from unobstructed perceptive knowledge (aesthetic contemplation) rather than from senses that directly excite desire or aversion. Greater degree of will-less knowing corresponds to higher æsthetic enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the beautiful
rubrics_metrics.description: A thing is beautiful when its form 'facilitates the knowledge of its Idea' so that the observer easily becomes the pure subject of knowledge without struggle—the object invites and sustains pure æsthetic contemplation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge objects by how readily they present their Idea and enable the observer to become 'objective' (free from individual will). Things that 'lend themselves to æsthetic contemplation' or 'make the transition from the individual thing to the Idea' more easily are more beautiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: The sublime occurs when objects have a hostile relation to the human will (threatening or overpowering) yet the beholder, by consciously detaching from will, contemplates their Idea and is raised above personal will—resulting in spiritual exaltation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify when aesthetic effect is produced not by ease of contemplation but by a conscious, forcible transcending of the will in presence of an object that is unfavourable or threatening to will. The sublime is accompanied by a continual remembrance of human volition in general (not a particular fear) and is lost if personal danger or willful action intrudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degrees and types of the sublime (dynamical vs mathematical)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are various degrees of the sublime and two main kinds: the dynamical (powerful, hostile forces of nature threatening the will) and the mathematical (immeasurable greatness in space or time which dwarfs the individual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both the intensity ('strong, bold, urgent' vs 'weak, distant') and the modality (threat/power vs immensity/age) of the object. Examples: storms, tempests, and towering waves are dynamical sublime; vast domes, starry heavens, high mountains, pyramids are mathematical sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition that sublime not become actual anxiety
rubrics_metrics.description: For the sublime impression to hold, the object must threaten or appear overpowering without producing actual personal pressure or immediate danger that would activate a particular volition and destroy contemplative peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that the spectator's safety or personal agency is not directly compromised; the feeling must be retained as contemplative transcendence (e.g., viewing a storm from a safe vantage rather than being caught in it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition from beautiful to sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects may produce a weak trace of sublime within beauty when there is some recollection of lack or threat to the will (e.g., cold light that does not warm), requiring a faint transcending of will to remain in pure knowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise gradations: subtle environmental cues (lack of warmth, desolate stillness) can nudge an otherwise beautiful perception toward the sublime by demanding a small act of will-detachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime character (ethical/aesthetic character)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sublime character is one in which 'the will is not excited by objects which are well calculated to excite it,' so that knowledge retains the upper hand; such a person observes people objectively without hatred, envy, or desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate moral/aesthetic character by the capacity to view others and events from a purely objective standpoint, resisting passion and appetitive responses (e.g., perceiving beauty without desire).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposite: the charming/attractive is anti-aesthetic
rubrics_metrics.description: The charming or attractive excites the will by presenting its fulfilment directly and thus draws the beholder away from pure contemplation; it is unworthy of art when it destroys æsthetic contemplation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage or critique artistic elements that deliberately stimulate appetite or desire (e.g., hyper-realistic food that makes one hungry; eroticised nudity intended to arouse) because they interrupt will-less knowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative species: disgusting/loathsome also inadmissible
rubrics_metrics.description: The disgusting or loathsome similarly arouses the will, but by active aversion, and is likewise inadmissible in art because it destroys pure æsthetic contemplation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish ugly (allowed) from disgusting (inadmissible); avoid imagery that provokes repulsion as it engages the will and defeats aesthetic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality of beauty but graded by ease of objective contemplation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every given thing may be aesthetically contemplated and thus 'beautiful' in principle, but some things are more beautiful because they make pure objective contemplation easier—either by clear expression of their Idea or by expressing a higher grade of objectivity of will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate beauty not by strict exclusion but by degree: consider how distinctly a thing reveals its Idea (clarity, completeness of form) and whether the Idea itself is of high significance (human form > lower material qualities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human form and action as highest aims of art
rubrics_metrics.description: Man is more beautiful than other objects because the revelation of his nature is the highest aim of art; human form and expression are the most important objects of plastic art, and human action of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise representations of human form and action when judging artistic ambition and depth, because they reveal the richest and most significant Ideas (higher grades of objectivity of will).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of æsthetic pleasure depends on object type
rubrics_metrics.description: In contemplation of inorganic/vegetable worlds or architecture the pleasure of will-less knowing predominates (lower grades of objectivity); in animals and man the pleasure consists more in comprehension of the Idea (richer content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor evaluative emphasis: for landscapes and buildings, consider the contemplative, perceptual qualities; for animals/humans, weigh expressive content, multiplicity of form, and depth of revealed will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matter as medium: art must reveal Ideas via material qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter itself cannot for its own sake express an Idea; rather the perceptible qualities of matter (gravity, rigidity, fluidity, light) are the phenomena through which Ideas reveal themselves. Manufactured articles express the Idea of their material ('forma substantialis') not their accidental form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess works by how effectively they exploit material qualities to disclose the underlying Idea. In crafts and architecture, critique whether form assists or hinders the material's expression of its essential qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural aesthetic principle: make the conflict of forces visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Architecture's æsthetic material is the conflict between gravity and rigidity; its aim (as fine art apart from utility) is to bring these low-grade Ideas into distinctness by lengthening and making visible their struggle (e.g., roof supported by columns, arches spanning, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate architecture on how clearly and variously it renders the interplay of gravity and rigidity (structural tension), and whether design choices demonstrate this conflict rather than merely serving utility. Poor or spoiled buildings hinder æsthetic contemplation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic contemplation requires suspension of causal/practical relations
rubrics_metrics.description: The knowledge of the Idea and the pure subject of knowing are 'entirely foreign to the principle of sufficient reason'—æsthetic experience presupposes that we do not follow relations to utility, causality, or individual will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing art, consider whether it allows (or obstructs) the observer to disengage from causal, temporal, or practical considerations and to apprehend the object as Idea (timeless, spaceless aspect). Objects that force consideration of external relations lessen æsthetic value.
